# ASVS 5.0 coverage mapping

Generated by `mapping/build-coverage.py` from `mapping/asvs-5.0-map.json` against [OWASP ASVS 5.0.0](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/releases/tag/v5.0.0_release) (`sha256:8201b20eec2908c3...`).

**Do not edit this file by hand.** Edit the map and regenerate.

## What this mapping does and does not claim

It claims: each control below was read against the ASVS requirements listed beside it, and those requirement ids exist in the released standard (the generator fails if one does not).

It does **not** claim ASVS compliance, alignment, or equivalence at any assurance level. A control that 'maps to' a requirement often covers part of it, occasionally states it more concretely, and sometimes is simply adjacent. Where ASVS is better, the note says so.

**Headline: 118 of 345 ASVS 5.0.0 requirements (34%) are touched by at least one of the 43 controls.** The other 227 (65%) are not, and the chapter table below says where.

## Coverage by ASVS chapter

| Chapter | Reqs | Touched | % | Controls | Assessment |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| V1 Encoding and Sanitization | 30 | 12 | 40% | 15, 16, 17, 18, 29, 31, 32, 33, 34 | Injection and encoding core is covered; the long tail (LDAP, XPath, LaTeX, ReDoS, CSV formula injection, memory safety) is not. |
| V2 Validation and Business Logic | 13 | 5 | 38% | 12, 15, 16, 26, 30, 42 | Input validation covered. Business-logic requirements (step order, transactions, resource locking, multi-user approval) are not. |
| V3 Web Frontend Security | 31 | 14 | 45% | 9, 17, 20, 21, 24 | Cookies, headers and CSRF covered. Not covered: DOM clobbering, postMessage, XSSI/JSONP, subresource integrity, redirect handling. |
| V4 API and Web Service | 16 | 4 | 25% | 21, 25, 27, 41 | Thin. HTTP request smuggling (V4.2) and WebSocket security (V4.4) are entirely absent from the controls. |
| V5 File Handling | 13 | 8 | 61% | 18, 25, 31 | Upload basics covered. Archive handling (zip bombs, symlinks, zip slip) and pixel-flood limits are not. |
| V6 Authentication | 47 | 5 | 10% | 11, 12, 13 | **Weakest area.** 47 requirements on authentication; the controls address password storage, brute-force and enumeration only. MFA, recovery flows and password policy detail are absent. |
| V7 Session Management | 19 | 4 | 21% | 6, 9, 13 | Session creation and termination covered. Inactivity and absolute timeouts, concurrent-session policy and step-up re-auth are not. |
| V8 Authorization | 13 | 6 | 46% | 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 29, 39, 40, 42 | Strongest area. Function, data and field-level authorization plus multi-tenancy all map directly. |
| V9 Self-contained Tokens | 7 | 6 | 85% | 13 | Near-complete. Control 13 covers self-contained token validation thoroughly. |
| V10 OAuth and OIDC | 36 | 8 | 22% | 14 | **Largest single gap by count.** 36 OAuth/OIDC requirements against one control. Anything doing real OAuth work must read V10 directly. |
| V11 Cryptography | 24 | 5 | 20% | 5, 10, 41 | Password hashing and cipher choice covered. Key lifecycle, crypto agility, constant-time operations and nonce reuse are not. |
| V12 Secure Communication | 12 | 2 | 16% | 21 | TLS for public traffic covered. mTLS, internal service-to-service TLS and certificate validation are not. |
| V13 Configuration | 21 | 14 | 66% | 1, 2, 3, 26, 27, 28, 32, 36, 39 | Well covered. V13.4 (unintended surface) is the single best-matched section in the standard. |
| V14 Data Protection | 13 | 5 | 38% | 1, 5, 9, 19 | Classification and minimisation covered. Retention schedules, caching controls and file-metadata stripping are not. |
| V15 Secure Coding and Architecture | 21 | 11 | 52% | 8, 19, 22, 23, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30, 32, 42 | Well covered - dependency management, mass assignment and field trimming all map directly. Concurrency (V15.4) does not. |
| V16 Security Logging and Error Handling | 17 | 9 | 52% | 19, 35, 36, 38 | Well covered. Audit trail and log hygiene map directly; log format and time-source requirements do not. |
| V17 WebRTC | 12 | 0 | 0% | — | **Zero coverage, by design.** WebRTC is out of scope for these controls entirely. |
| **Total** | **345** | **118** | **34%** | | |

## Control-by-control map

Tiers describe how a control can be checked, not how important it is:

- **Tier 1** — PR gate - static, no running app
- **Tier 2** — Post-deploy probe - needs a deployed URL
- **Tier 3** — Test-suite contract - the consuming project writes it
- **Tier 4** — Attested manual - the control is the date


### Group A

| # | Control | Tier | ASVS 5.0 | Note |
| ---: | --- | :---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Hide API keys | 1 | `V13.3.1`, `V13.3.2`, `V14.3.3` | ASVS treats this as secrets management generally; the control is narrower and sharper - no secret in a client bundle, and NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ vars are public identifiers only. |
| 2 | Purge Git secrets | 1 | `V13.3.1`, `V13.3.4`, `V13.4.1` | PARTIAL. V13.4.1 covers not deploying .git metadata; V13.3.4 covers rotation. ASVS 5.0 has no requirement to scan or scrub version-control history for committed secrets. The rotate-then-scrub ordering is not in the standard. |
| 3 | Use the public/anon key client-side | 1 | `V13.3.2`, `V8.3.1` | Least-privilege secret access, specialised to the BaaS anon-vs-service-role split that ASVS does not name. |

### Group B

| # | Control | Tier | ASVS 5.0 | Note |
| ---: | --- | :---: | --- | --- |
| 4 | Enable row-level security | 3 | `V8.2.2`, `V8.3.1`, `V8.4.1` | ASVS states the outcome (data-specific access restricted at a trusted service layer); the control names the mechanism (RLS enabled AND a policy present) and the ORM-only fallback. |
| 5 | Encrypt sensitive data | 4 | `V14.1.1`, `V14.1.2`, `V14.2.4`, `V11.3.2`, `V11.3.3` | ASVS V11 is substantially deeper here - key lifecycle, crypto agility, authenticated encryption modes. The control covers column-level at-rest encryption only. |
| 6 | Enforce server-side auth | 3 | `V8.3.1`, `V8.2.1`, `V7.2.1` | Direct match. |
| 7 | Lock record access (IDOR) | 3 | `V8.2.2` | Direct match. V8.2.2 names IDOR explicitly. |
| 8 | Block field tampering (mass assignment) | 3 | `V15.3.3`, `V8.2.3` | Direct match. V8.2.3 covers the authorization side (broken object property level authorization), V15.3.3 the coding side. |

ASVS scopes itself to the application under verification and has no requirement that preview/staging deploys carry auth, a noindex header, separate credentials, or non-production data. This control has no real ASVS counterpart. |

### Group I

| # | Control | Tier | ASVS 5.0 | Note |
| ---: | --- | :---: | --- | --- |
| 35 | Keep an audit trail | 4 | `V16.3.1`, `V16.3.2`, `V16.2.1`, `V16.4.2`, `V16.1.1` | Direct match. ASVS V16 is more thorough on log format, time synchronisation and log inventory. |
| 36 | Keep secrets out of logs - and logs out of public reach | 1 | `V16.2.5`, `V16.4.2`, `V16.4.1`, `V16.5.1`, `V13.4.5` | Direct match. |
| 37 | Back up, and prove the restore | 4 | **none** | NO ASVS COVERAGE. ASVS 5.0 contains no backup or restore requirement - it verifies the application, not the operational practice around it. V14.2.7 covers retention and deletion, which is the opposite concern. This control has no counterpart in the standard. |
| 38 | Monitor and alert | 4 | `V16.4.3` | PARTIAL. V16.4.3 requires logs be shipped to a separate system for detection and alerting. Nothing in ASVS requires proving an alert actually reaches a human, which is this control's entire verification step. |
| 39 | Run everything least-privilege | 4 | `V13.3.2`, `V13.2.3`, `V8.4.2` | PARTIAL. ASVS covers least privilege for secret access and non-default service credentials. Database grants, cloud IAM scoping, firewall default-deny and SSH key-only are infrastructure, which ASVS deliberately excludes. |
| 40 | Isolate tenants | 3 | `V8.4.1` | Direct match, and ASVS states it in one requirement. The control adds the operational surfaces that leak quietly - cache keys, search indexes, background jobs, file paths. |
| 41 | Verify webhooks | 3 | `V4.1.5`, `V11.2.4` | PARTIAL GAP. V4.1.5 covers per-message digital signatures at L3 only; V11.2.4 covers constant-time comparison. ASVS has no requirement for webhook replay windows, event-id idempotency, or verifying over the raw pre-parse body. |
| 42 | Keep payment authority on the server | 3 | `V2.2.2`, `V2.3.2`, `V8.3.1`, `V15.3.3` | PARTIAL. ASVS handles this as generic business-logic validation at a trusted service layer. It has no payment-specific requirement, so price tampering, coupon re-validation at charge time and webhook-as-source-of-truth are specialisations, not restatements. |
| 43 | Make the security gate unbypassable | 1 | **none** | NO ASVS COVERAGE. Searched the released standard for pipeline, CI/CD, branch, version control, merge, code review and commit: zero requirements match. The two near-hits are different concerns - V13.4.1 covers not deploying .git metadata, V15.2.4 covers component provenance. ASVS verifies the application, not the pipeline that ships it, so every CI-enforced control in this protocol rests on an assumption the standard never states. |

## Controls with no ASVS counterpart

- **37. Back up, and prove the restore** — NO ASVS COVERAGE. ASVS 5.0 contains no backup or restore requirement - it verifies the application, not the operational practice around it. V14.2.7 covers retention and deletion, which is the opposite concern. This control has no counterpart in the standard.
- **43. Make the security gate unbypassable** — NO ASVS COVERAGE. Searched the released standard for pipeline, CI/CD, branch, version control, merge, code review and commit: zero requirements match. The two near-hits are different concerns - V13.4.1 covers not deploying .git metadata, V15.2.4 covers component provenance. ASVS verifies the application, not the pipeline that ships it, so every CI-enforced control in this protocol rests on an assumption the standard never states.

## Automation feasibility

| Tier | What it means | Controls | Count |
| :---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 | PR gate - static, no running app | 1, 2, 3, 15, 17, 22, 23, 31, 33, 34, 36, 43 | 12 |
| 2 | Post-deploy probe - needs a deployed URL | 9, 20, 21, 27, 28 | 5 |
| 3 | Test-suite contract - the consuming project writes it | 4, 6, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 19, 24, 25, 26, 29, 30, 32, 40, 41, 42 | 19 |
| 4 | Attested manual - the control is the date | 5, 10, 12, 35, 37, 38, 39 | 7 |

**17 of 43 controls (39%) can be checked by CI this repository can ship.** The remaining 26 are a contract with the consuming project (Tier 3) or an action someone takes and dates (Tier 4). Automating the automatable subset and being explicit about the rest is the honest position; a green pipeline is evidence about Tiers 1 and 2 and nothing else.
